title: Stable nucleus (Skein energy minimum)
html:
Definition. Stable nucleus (Skein energy minimum)

A stable nucleus is a multi-nucleon Hopf link that extremizes the Skein binding Lagrangian (Skein binding Lagrangian).

Let \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{n} be the categorical proton and neutron (categorical proton, categorical neutron). A nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons is the iterated Hopf link. (Here Z is the atomic number, the standard nuclear physics notation for the proton count, freeing p for use as a brane point.)

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  = 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{p} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{p}}_{Z}
   \oplus 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{n} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{n}}_{N}.

The nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is stable if (Z, N) is a critical point of the Skein binding Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} (Skein binding Lagrangian) under beta variation (exchange of \mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{n} at fixed A = Z + N):

  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}}{\partial Z}
  \bigg|_{A}
  = 0
  \qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad
  Z = \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)},

where a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C and a_A is the Pauli coefficient (beta-stability).

A stable atom appends Z electrons:

  \mathcal{A}(Z, N)
  = 
  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)  \oplus  Z \cdot T_{2,3}.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. We invoke real- and complex-analytic constructs, including real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, and numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities we draw upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
